name: Bal Mithai
description: A brown, chocolate-like fudge of roasted khoya coated in tiny white sugar-coated poppy-seed balls. It is the best-known sweet of Kumaon, and Almora is the place most associated with it.
how_to_eat: Eat a piece as is; the sugar balls give it crunch.
how_to_order: Ask for bal mithai by weight at sweet shops in Almora's bazaar; it travels well as a gift.

name: Singori
description: Thickened, flavoured khoya, sometimes with coconut, wrapped in a cone of maalu leaf. It began as a delicacy of Old Tehri under the Panwar dynasty and is now strongly identified with Almora and Kumaon.
how_to_eat: Unwrap the leaf cone and eat the sweet inside; the leaf is not eaten.
how_to_order: Ask for singori by the piece at Almora sweet shops, usually sold alongside bal mithai.

name: Kafuli
description: A thick green curry of spinach and fenugreek leaves, thickened with rice or wheat flour and often finished with yogurt or buttermilk. Traditionally cooked in an iron pot, it is a signature dish of Uttarakhand, favoured in Garhwal.
how_to_eat: Eat it with steamed rice or mandua roti.
how_to_order: Ask for kafuli with rice at pahadi-food restaurants and homestays.

name: Phaanu
description: A Garhwali stew of one or several lentils soaked overnight, ground to a paste and slow-cooked for hours to a soupy consistency with minimal spices.
how_to_eat: Eat it with steamed rice.
how_to_order: Ask for phaanu-bhaat at Garhwali home kitchens or pahadi-food restaurants.

name: Chainsoo
description: Black urad dal roasted, ground and cooked in ghee with onion, tomato and spices. A Garhwali dish also made in Kumaon, it is often cooked in iron vessels and eaten especially in winter.
how_to_eat: Eat it with steamed rice.
how_to_order: Ask for chainsoo (also called chaunsu) with rice at pahadi-food restaurants.

name: Bhatt ki Churkani
description: A Kumaoni curry of bhatt (black soybean) blended with rice flour, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric and chilli. Bhatt is a key crop of Kumaon.
how_to_eat: Eat it with rice, garnished with coriander.
how_to_order: Ask for bhatt ki churkani with rice at Kumaoni restaurants.

name: Bhatt ka Jaula
description: A simple Kumaoni porridge of bhatt (black soybean) and rice cooked together without spices.
how_to_eat: Eat it with kadhi or a pinch of green coriander salt.

name: Aloo ke Gutke
description: Parboiled pahadi potatoes cut into pieces and fried with basic spices. Called the fast food of Kumaon, it is sold hot at tea stalls and eaten at Holi.
how_to_eat: Eat it hot with bhang ki chutney and tea.
how_to_order: Ask for aloo ke gutke at tea stalls in Kumaoni towns.

name: Bhang ki Chutney
description: A tangy paste of roasted hemp seeds ground with green chilli, lemon juice, mint, coriander and salt. It accompanies many Kumaoni snacks.
how_to_eat: Eat it as a dip with aloo ke gutke, parathas or pakoras.
how_to_order: Ask for bhang ki chutney on the side when ordering aloo ke gutke or gahat paratha.

name: Kumaoni Raita
description: Curd mixed with grated cucumber, fenugreek seeds and turmeric. It is a staple side dish served with most Kumaoni meals.
how_to_eat: Eat it alongside rice, dal and rotis.
how_to_order: Ask for pahadi or Kumaoni raita with a thali.

name: Mandua ki Roti
description: Flatbread of mandua (finger millet) flour, sometimes kneaded with yogurt, carrot, chilli and spring onion. It is an everyday hill staple; koda rotis are also eaten with ghee and jaggery.
how_to_eat: Eat it with kafuli, bhatt ki dal or ghee and jaggery.
how_to_order: Ask for mandua roti or koda roti at pahadi restaurants.

name: Gahat Paratha
description: Whole-wheat parathas or chapatis stuffed with spiced cooked gahat (horse gram). It is a classic hill breakfast.
how_to_eat: Eat it with bhang chutney, cucumber raita or butter.
how_to_order: Ask for gahat ka paratha at breakfast in homestays and pahadi cafes.

name: Gahat Soup
description: A warming soup of gahat (horse gram) dal cooked with ginger, garlic and garam masala, sometimes enriched with cream. Horse gram is a key pulse of the hills.
how_to_eat: Drink it hot as a starter or with rice.
how_to_order: Ask for gahat soup or gahat ki dal at pahadi restaurants.

name: Thechwani
description: Mountain radish and potatoes crushed on a stone grinder, then cooked with garlic, ginger and spices into a curry.
how_to_eat: Eat it with mandua roti, puri or rice.
how_to_order: Ask for thechwani at Kumaoni restaurants.

name: Dubuk
description: A winter dal from the Garhwal foothills of ground gahat or bhatt, part shaped into dumplings and the rest cooked into a thin gravy, tempered with cumin, fenugreek and hing.
how_to_eat: Eat it mostly with rice, sometimes with roti.

name: Kandali ka Saag
description: A saag of stinging nettle (bichhu ghas) leaves cooked with spices and sometimes lentils. It is a Garhwali hill green.
how_to_eat: Eat it with rice or mandua roti.

name: Ras Bhaat (Thatwani)
description: A Kumaoni winter dish of mixed pulses such as chana, bhatt, rajma and gahat boiled together; the broth is thickened with rice flour and tempered with cumin.
how_to_eat: Eat it hot over rice, with the pulses on the side or mixed in.

name: Sana Hua Nimbu
description: A winter snack of large hill lemons and radish mixed with curd, salt and bhang seed powder.
how_to_eat: Eat it from a bowl as a tangy snack, often in the winter sun.

name: Rasmi Badi
description: Lentil dumplings (badi) cooked in a yogurt-based curry. It is a Kumaoni dish.
how_to_eat: Eat it with rice.

name: Arsa
description: A fried sweet of rice flour and jaggery. In Garhwal it is served at weddings and given as a return gift.
how_to_eat: Eat it at room temperature as a snack with tea.
how_to_order: Ask for arsa at sweet shops in Garhwali towns, especially in the wedding season.

name: Jhangore ki Kheer
description: A pudding of jhangora (barnyard millet) cooked in milk with sugar and cardamom. It is a hill alternative to rice kheer.
how_to_eat: Eat it warm or chilled with a spoon.
how_to_order: Ask for jhangora kheer at pahadi restaurants.

name: Baadi
description: A thick, dough-like dish of ragi (finger millet) flour cooked with water and ghee.
how_to_eat: Eat it with gahat ki dal or phaanu.

name: Buransh Sharbat
description: A deep-red drink made from the flowers of Rhododendron arboreum (buransh), which bloom across the Uttarakhand hills. Burans Sharbat received a GI tag in 2023.
how_to_eat: Dilute the squash with cold water and drink it chilled.
how_to_order: Ask for buransh juice or squash at shops and government outlets in hill towns; it is sold bottled.
